interface.signature: def solve(M: int, N: int, K: int) -> int:

preconditions.description: Input dimensions M (rows), N (columns), and K (max integer value) must satisfy the given constraints.

preconditions.expression: isinstance(M, int) and isinstance(N, int) and isinstance(K, int)
preconditions.description: M, N, and K must be integers.

postconditions.description: The result is a non-negative integer less than the modulus 998244353.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= K for x in [1, 2, 3, 4]) if M == 2 and N == 2 and K == 2 else True
postconditions.description: For the sample input (2, 2, 2), the output must match the expected value 873463811 modulo 998244353.

postconditions.expression: solve(M, N, K) == (P * pow(Q, -1, 998244353)) % 998244353 for some integers P, Q where Q != 0 and gcd(Q, 998244353) == 1
postconditions.description: The result is the modular inverse of Q multiplied by P, where the expected value of SCCs is P/Q in reduced form.

postconditions.expression: solve(M, N, K) == (sum((probability * num_sccs) for num_sccs, probability in enumerate(scc_distribution)) % 998244353) if M == 2 and N == 2 and K == 2 else True
postconditions.description: The result is the expected value of SCCs computed as the sum over all possible matrix configurations of (number of SCCs * probability of that configuration), modulo 998244353.
